body: Kelly criterion: for a bet with win probability p and payoff odds b, the growth-maximising fraction of capital is f = (bp - q)/b, where q = 1 - p. Thorp's practice: (1) bet only where expectation is demonstrably positive (counted cards, mispriced warrants/convertibles); (2) size at a fraction of Kelly (half or less) because inputs are uncertain and full Kelly produces brutal drawdowns - roughly a 50% chance of halving the bankroll at some point; (3) hedge out risks you are not paid for (market-neutral). Translation for a stock investor: edge estimates are noisy, so practical position caps (e.g., 5-10% at cost for high conviction, 1-3% for speculative) approximate fractional Kelly; never use leverage or F&O sizes that can wipe you out (see SEBI's F&O loss studies). Feasibility test (Thorp's Madoff insight): if a track record is too smooth for the claimed strategy, verify it or walk away. Evidence quality: Kelly is mathematically proven for repeated bets with known odds; real markets violate those assumptions, which is why fractional Kelly is the rule.
title: Thorp: quantified edge and fractional Kelly sizing
